description: Meshy 7.1 generates 3D models from a single image, with standard, low-poly, and Smart Topology modes, optional textures and PBR maps, and geometry resolution up to 4K.

input_params.name: topology
input_params.description: Specify the topology of the generated model. Quad for smooth surfaces, Triangle for detailed geometry.

input_params.name: ultra_mode
input_params.description: Deprecated: use geometry_resolution='2k'. If both fields are provided, geometry_resolution takes precedence.

input_params.name: rigging_height_meters
input_params.description: Approximate height of the character in meters. Only used when enable_rigging is true.

input_params.name: texture_prompt
input_params.description: Text prompt to guide the texturing process

input_params.name: is_a_t_pose
input_params.description: Deprecated: use pose_mode instead. When true, generates a T-pose model.

input_params.name: should_remesh
input_params.description: Whether to enable the remesh phase

input_params.name: geometry_resolution
input_params.description: Geometry resolution. 4k is only available with Meshy-7.1.

input_params.name: target_polycount
input_params.description: Target number of polygons in the generated model. When model_type is 'smart-topology' and this is left unset, Meshy's lower smart-topology default (4,000) is used instead; smart topology accepts at most 15,000.

input_params.name: symmetry_mode
input_params.description: Controls symmetry behavior during model generation. Off disables symmetry, Auto determines it automatically, On enforces symmetry.

input_params.name: enable_rigging
input_params.description: Automatically rig the generated model as a humanoid character. Includes basic walking and running animations. Best results with humanoid characters that have clearly defined limbs.

input_params.name: pose_mode
input_params.description: Pose mode for the generated model. 'a-pose' generates an A-pose, 't-pose' generates a T-pose, empty string for no specific pose.

input_params.name: animation_action_id
input_params.description: Animation preset ID from Meshy's library. Only used when enable_animation is true; in that case it must be in [0, 696] (``0`` is the "Idle" preset) and is otherwise rejected with a 422. See https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/animation-library for available action IDs.

input_params.name: model_type
input_params.description: Type of 3D mesh generation. 'standard' produces a regular high-detail mesh; 'lowpoly' produces a low-poly mesh optimized for cleaner polygons; 'smart-topology' uses Meshy-T2 for clean, natively separated parts. When set to 'lowpoly', the remesh controls (topology, target_polycount, should_remesh) are ignored by Meshy.

input_params.name: image_url
input_params.description: Image URL or base64 data URI for 3D model creation. Supports .jpg, .jpeg, and .png formats. Also supports AVIF and HEIF formats which will be automatically converted.

input_params.name: enable_safety_checker
input_params.description: If set to true, input data will be checked for safety before processing.

input_params.name: texture_image_url
input_params.description: 2D image to guide the texturing process

input_params.name: enable_pbr
input_params.description: Generate PBR Maps (metallic, roughness, normal) in addition to base color

input_params.name: enable_animation
input_params.description: Apply an animation preset to the rigged model. Requires enable_rigging to be true.

output_fields.name: texture_urls
output_fields.description: Array of texture file objects, matching Meshy API structure

output_fields.name: basic_animations
output_fields.description: Basic walking and running animations. Only present when enable_rigging is true.

output_fields.name: rig_task_id
output_fields.description: Rigging task ID. Only present when enable_rigging is true.

output_fields.name: rigged_character_fbx
output_fields.description: Rigged character in FBX format. Only present when enable_rigging is true.

output_fields.name: rigged_character_glb
output_fields.description: Rigged character in GLB format. Only present when enable_rigging is true.

output_fields.name: seed
output_fields.description: The seed used for generation (if available)

output_fields.name: animation_glb
output_fields.description: Animated 3D model in GLB format. Only present when enable_animation is true.

output_fields.name: thumbnail
output_fields.description: Preview thumbnail of the generated model

output_fields.name: animation_fbx
output_fields.description: Animated 3D model in FBX format. Only present when enable_animation is true.

selection_guidance:
Before choosing a model for a new operation, call recommend_model with the user's task and constraints unless the user named a model or explicitly requested a model set/comparison. Reuse that recommendation for the operation; do not repeatedly request the same recommendation.
For an explicit set/comparison, use list_model_sets to resolve the requested operation and sets, then use its exact returned endpoint IDs within the user's requested scope. Read each selected model's live schema and applicable published guidance, build its input from the user's brief and references, and preserve required settings. Explain incompatible or unavailable members instead of silently replacing them, approximating settings, or running the rest of a large set. Set membership is discovery, never authorization or proof of task fit.
Honor an explicitly requested model; verify its exact endpoint and do not silently substitute it.
Copy endpoint_id exactly from the live catalog. Namespaces and versions vary by provider: never add or change a provider prefix, invent an endpoint from a model name, or reuse a guessed alias. When a named model is missing or unavailable, search_models can resolve current catalog matches; explain any mismatch with the requested endpoint before choosing a replacement. An unavailable endpoint alone does not establish that the user connected the wrong account.
Otherwise use current applicable published guidance in recommended_model and model_knowledge after checking the user's real sources, required capabilities and scoped budget. Follow the next compatible published fallback and explain why. If published guidance is missing or outdated, use search_models and search_docs to evaluate current candidates. A new endpoint can qualify without adoption statistics, but recency alone does not establish quality. Do not submit a choice with decision_status needs_input, no_compatible_candidate or evidence_unavailable. A workflow_needed result needs a verified dependent plan before spend.
With draft_inspection_required, draft_candidate establishes technical/reference fit only. Generate a draft only within existing user authorization and the checked budget, then inspect it against original conditioning sources before dependent generation or approval. Preservation stays unverified; a draft candidate is not a final recommended_model or permission to spend.
Catalog order, popularity and release recency are discovery signals, not quality or latency rankings. Fast subject motion describes movement in the scene, not generation latency. Only treat user-requested settings as hard constraints; do not invent an exact resolution or audio requirement to justify switching models.
Live retrieval does not establish when guidance was authored. Without an update date, freshness is unknown; verify capabilities in current schemas/docs and do not claim the pick is the newest or fastest without evidence. Skills and workflow examples supply production advice, not competing model defaults. Prefer current published task/domain guidance over bundled family rankings. Use get_pricing for the actual settings before material spending. Cost estimates preserve units and cover only known quantities, not final billing guarantees. Pass the optional decision_id to run_model, submit_job or each applicable batch item; it links observations and is never authorization.

evidence.latency_definition: Successful execution observations in milliseconds; mixed workloads; excludes queue/startup; not runtime guarantees.
evidence.instructions: Successful execution observations in milliseconds; mixed workloads; excludes queue/startup; not runtime guarantees. Report p50/p90 with their measurement window. Null means unknown, never zero. Trending is the analytics category rank at its source timestamp, not adoption or quality. New means registry publication within 30 days of the response evaluation time, not first usage. Lab recommendations are authored guidance, not measured latency, trending or newness. Use the existing pricing tool for current prices, preserving billing units and required configuration; these observations contain no prices.
